A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the group A arboviruses (togaviruses) are able to replicate and produce antigen in cells enucleate at any time after infection while group B arboviruses require the presence of a nucleus at least 2 h postinfection.
the group B togaviruses have an initial requirement for a nucleus-associated process, whereas the group A togaviruses do not.

The main takeaway from our work is that
enucleation of cells is a powerful technique for studying the nuclear requirements of viruses.
the nuclear requirement is not a general property of togaviruses but is specific for group B togaviruses.
